repair: REPAIR 7 -- what the notebook 05 arms do and do not establish

A.purpose: faithful replication of the published protocol's defect
A.protocol: SMOTE-ENN over the whole subset, then split 60/40
A.test_set: resampled: about 50 percent fraud, largely synthetic positives, ENN-cleaned
supports: that the published protocol produces about 0.99 precision
that a balanced test set larger than the stated training set is arithmetically implied by the reported numbers

B.purpose: the Arm A models scored on real data at natural prevalence
B.protocol: same fitted models, clean held-out rows never in the subset
B.status: VALID as a demonstration that the Arm A numbers do not transfer

C.purpose: resampling applied correctly, to the training partition only
C.protocol: split first, SMOTE-ENN the training partition, test untouched

confounds_in_the_A_to_B_contrast: base rate changes from about 50 percent to 0.129 percent
Arm A positives are largely synthetic SMOTE interpolations, not real transactions
ENN has removed borderline examples from both classes, making the Arm A test set easier
resample-then-split places points interpolated from training rows into the test set
permitted_claim: Precision measured on a resampled test set does not transfer to natural prevalence, so the published protocol's reported precision is not an estimate of deployed precision.
claim_NOT_supported: That evaluation prevalence alone accounts for the collapse, or that any specific share of it is attributable to prevalence rather than to syntheticness, ENN cleaning, or train/test contamination.
experiment_that_would_settle_it: An Arm D varying only the evaluation base rate: one fixed model, one fixed threshold, the same real positives throughout, with real negatives subsampled to 50, 10, 1 and 0.129 percent. No synthetic points, no ENN, no retraining. Deferred to the next research phase; not run here.
attribution_to_SMOTE_or_RUS: Not made. The current design cannot separate the resampling method from the evaluation base rate.
